paragraphs: Friend, here's what I love about the end of Job's story. The LORD says Job spoke about Him accurately, and He calls Job "My servant Job" again and again (Job 42:7-8). Job didn't have all the answers, and he never got a tidy explanation for his suffering. What the LORD cared about was that Job brought Him the truth, even when it was hard to say.

Now look at what the LORD asks Job to do. The friends who got it wrong come to Job, and the LORD says, "My servant Job will pray for you" (Job 42:8). After Job prayed for his friends, the LORD restored his prosperity (Job 42:10). I can't promise you every hard season ends with doubled blessings in this life. But I can tell you what the text shows: the LORD heard Job's prayer, and He is the One who restores.

So here's the big idea, baker. You can bring God your honest questions, your pain and your praying, and He doesn't turn you away. The same LORD who stayed with Job in the hard part is the One who "blessed Job's latter days more than his first" (Job 42:12). Keep your ovens warm and keep trusting Him, friend, because He knows how to finish a story. Job's story is done, but there's a whole Word of God out there still waiting on you.
